summary.text: A 15-year-old girl presented to a child and adolescent psychiatry clinic, referred from rheumatology, with depressive symptoms. Pain began in her lower extremities at age 4 and later generalized; low mood began at age 10 after a move and bullying at a new school. She was diagnosed with juvenile-onset fibromyalgia a year before the clinic visit.

Clinic assessment found she fulfilled DSM-5 criteria for early onset persistent depressive disorder with intermittent major depressive episodes and a current episode. She also had vitamin D deficiency and iron deficiency anemia, corrected with supplements and ferrous fumarate, and she had no known drug allergies.

A combined approach was used: duloxetine started at 30 mg orally daily, with nausea and headache, then raised to 60 mg, plus interpersonal psychotherapy for adolescents with initial, middle and termination phases over 4, 7 and 4 sessions. A stepwise plan for pain and exhaustion flare-ups was developed. Symptoms shifted to full remission towards the end of the middle phase.

At a booster session one month after the final IPT-A session she reported continued remission of depressive symptoms. Because of fatigability, pain and academic stress, duloxetine was increased to 90 mg orally daily, and she continues on it. At every-3-month follow-ups her fibromyalgia symptoms were well managed with occasional stress-related flare-ups.
